business_value.instructions: Assess Evidence of value to the intended business user for the project in `project`, using actual `files`, `evaluation`, `known_gaps` and `verification`. Rate only evidence present, not planned controls. Code and evidence override README claims. Missing representative deployment evidence cannot be assumed. This question assesses business_value; do not conflate cosmetic names or test counts with achieved user value.
criteria: No defined user decision or business output.
A defined user and plausible task exist; evidence is limited to examples and assumptions.
A working end-to-end task has independently reviewed synthetic outcomes; no representative user trial measures value.
Representative users measured improved task outcomes against their current process, including regressions and review effort.
Repeated representative deployments show sustained measured benefits with named owners and monitored regressions.

criteria: Known failures can silently produce incorrect authoritative decisions.
Only happy-path examples are demonstrated; important business invariants are unchecked.
Business invariants and failure states have automated tests plus reviewed model outputs; representative domain coverage remains missing.
Independent domain-labeled representative cases and adversarial cases meet predeclared error tolerances; regressions are enforced.
Production outcomes and change evaluations confirm those tolerances over time, including uncommon and high-impact cases.

criteria: No runnable setup or usable input/output contract.
A developer can run a canned example but an operator cannot follow a documented real-data path.
Documented installation, validated file contracts and usable output enable a manual export/import trial; live source integration is unverified.
An authorized source adapter and operator journey are tested against a representative sandbox with identity, provenance and freshness preserved.
Operators have repeatedly completed onboarding, error recovery and routine use in target environments with maintained connectors.

criteria: Routine errors can be hidden as success or cause uncontrolled execution.
Failures are visible but resource bounds or failure recovery tests are missing.
Bounded requests, explicit failures and transport tests exist; sustained workload, restart recovery or operational observation remain unverified.
Deployment-specific load, fault, timeout, restart and recovery tests meet declared service objectives with actionable telemetry.
An operated service meets recorded objectives over time with tested rollback, recovery drills and accountable incident ownership.

criteria: Known exploitable critical access or data disclosure defect is unresolved.
Controls are mostly stated in documentation; implemented trust boundaries are not tested.
Implemented local/provider trust boundaries are tested and deployment exclusions explicit; target identity, authorization and data-governance validation are missing.
Target identity and authorization boundaries, retention, secrets and provider approval are independently tested in the intended environment.
Ongoing security ownership, vulnerability handling and recurring tests demonstrate those deployment controls remain effective.

criteria: Untraceable generated assertions are presented as completed business actions.
Output requests human review but lacks usable links to the evidence or execution.
Output records evidence and execution provenance with explicit uncertainty; review decisions and freshness invalidation are not durably enforced.
Review decisions are bound to the exact work product and source versions, durably recorded, and invalidated on changed or ineligible evidence; the stated reviewer identity boundary is enforced.
The review lifecycle and authorized source freshness are verified end-to-end in the target business system, including audit retrieval and revocation.

criteria: Only names, styling or branding distinguish a copied generic demonstration.
A repository-specific design or constraint is described but its practical improvement is not demonstrated.

A reproducible comparison against a relevant existing alternative demonstrates a useful improvement and honestly reports tradeoffs.
Independent adopters reproduce the comparative improvement on representative tasks and the capability remains maintained.

criteria: Known required attribution is removed or fabricated ownership, deployments or results are claimed.
Origin or maturity statements are ambiguous and supporting artifacts are absent.
Origin, implementation scope and limits are stated with linked code and test artifacts; some material claims remain unverified.
Material implementation and evaluation claims are traceable, limitations explicit, and applicable source notices retained; no evidence of fabricated claims.
Independent provenance and claim audit verifies all material claims and required notices against reproducible records.

first_priority.instructions: For the project in `project`, which single next improvement most directly removes its current barrier to useful enterprise adoption, based on files and known_gaps? This is prioritization, not production approval.

criteria.business_correctness: Fix an actual incorrect or unsafe business result or source association.
criteria.source_integration: Establish authorized, identity-preserving source ingestion and freshness in a representative sandbox.
criteria.review_lifecycle: Implement durable content-bound human review and invalidation of stale decisions.
criteria.operational_controls: Implement and test missing runtime deadline, recovery, operational trace or deployment boundary.
criteria.representative_validation: Measure value and error rates on independent representative user cases against an existing process.
criteria.evidence_insufficient: Supplied evidence cannot support choosing a priority.
